translation.text: And the middle one reached to heaven, like the throne of the Lord, made of a stone called puk;[a] and the top of the throne was of sapphire stone.[b]

footnotes.text: Puk transliterates the uncertain printed stone name. The earlier English crystal is not established by this scan review; no precise mineral identification is claimed.

The first consonant of the word in this upper-part phrase is unclear in the selected photograph. POB marks that single source glyph with⟦?⟧; Charles did not print this marker. The earlier y-reading and a possible d-reading are not certified. Top or upper part is a provisional rendering supported by the actual Dillmann1865column1085 lexical entry, which includes a throne and cites18:8; that meaning does not settle the printed glyph. Sapphire remains in this phrase, not an invented foundation. No fresh manuscript collation or all-glyph resolution is claimed.
